_what: Per-question decisions for the July-2024 MES (Combined) General Studies import: keep-or-drop, GS syllabus unit and leaf sub-topic, and a one-line explanation of the keyed answer.
_split_policy: Static GK only, the same rule as the other three sittings. Every drop keeps its reason here and the importer prints them all on every run, so pulling one back is a one-field edit - as July-2023 Q82 proved when unit 10 gained the leaf it needed.
_drops: 14 of 100: ten time-bound (Q3, Q5, Q6, Q12, Q15, Q24, Q26, Q30, Q45, Q46 - two office holders, four annual awards or mascots, a named-date unveiling, a one-Games forecast and a growth-rate projection) and four off-syllabus (Q75, Q76, Q78, Q79).
_a_third_syllabus_gap_worth_a_decision: The four off-syllabus drops are all SOCIAL AND CRIMINAL LEGISLATION: the RPwD Act's count of disabilities, the Juvenile Justice Act's definition of a juvenile, the imprisonment threshold for a heinous offence, and the fact that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC of 1860. None fits a leaf of units 1-11. Note what this is: the THIRD distinct gap the derived unit list has shown, after the communication/management block (which became unit 11) and the number-system/mensuration gap (which became two unit-10 leaves). The Q79 fact in particular is durable and important. A 'Laws and social legislation' unit or a set of leaves under unit 1 is the obvious fix, but that is a scope decision for the user rather than something to slip into an import - so these four are dropped with their reasons on record and are one field edit from coming back. Q72 and Q77 are KEPT because education law has a home: both are Article 21A, a fundamental right.
_key_quality:
The key was settled before the questions were transcribed - two documents (provisional 10 July and final 12 September 2024), two independent by-eye reads agreeing 100/100, a geometry-based machine read, and zoom on every conflict. A third independent eye read on 2026-09-02, after the questions were transcribed, again agreed 100/100, as did a re-read of the provisional page. Checked against the questions, the key is right everywhere - NO genuine errors. Q54 and Q93 are keyed defensibly but loosely and say so on the card.

CORRECTION 2026-09-02: this field previously claimed 'ONE genuine error: Q94 keys the President as administering the Governor's oath, where Article 159 plainly requires the Chief Justice of the High Court', and Q94's explanation was written as 'CONTESTED - the key looks wrong... do not learn this one'. Both were mistaken about what the key says. Q94's official answer is (D) 'Chief Justice of High Court' - which is exactly what Article 159 requires - not (B) 'President'. Whoever tagged it read the key letter as B. The card would have told the user to distrust a correct answer and to believe MPSC had keyed the President, so this was a wrong-answer-teaching bug rather than a cosmetic one. The explanation now just states Article 159 plainly. Worth generalising: an exp that disputes its own key is a signal to re-read the key letter FIRST, before believing the exp. The importer now prints every such exp on each run with the keyed option's text beside it, which is what would have made this obvious immediately.
_source_misprints: The paper misprints its own option letters twice - Q81 as (a)(b)(c)(c) and Q90 as (a)(b)(b)(d). The parser assigns the four bracketed markers POSITIONALLY, so both land correctly and both keys point at the right text; recorded on those two cards rather than silently corrected. Source typos are also preserved verbatim: Q11 'Environmnent', Q71 'Tocopherpol', Q72 'Righ', Q75 'Disabilites', Q78 'offcences'.

tags.sub: Judiciary: Supreme Court, High Courts, judicial review

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. SHRESHTA places bright SC students from poor households in top private residential schools. Which ministry owns a scheme is fixed by its design.

tags.sub: Biology: cell, tissues, human body systems

tags.sub: Biology: cell, tissues, human body systems
tags.exp: Lysozyme, which breaks down bacterial cell walls and so gives saliva and tears a first line of defence. Ribozymes are catalytic RNA and lipase digests fat - neither is antibacterial.
The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, India's first, spanning Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.
The IUCN, which maintains the Red List of Threatened Species. WWF and UNEP work on conservation but publish no such list, which is the distinction being tested.

tags.sub: National current affairs of the preceding 12-18 months

tags.sub: Cyber security and cyber crime awareness
tags.exp: SAMBHAV - Secure Army Mobile Bharat Version, an end-to-end encrypted handset ecosystem for Army communications. A codename is fixed.
Argentina, where India's KABIL signed a 2024 agreement for lithium brine exploration in Catamarca - India's first such overseas lithium deal.

Years of schooling. India's National MPI uses twelve indicators across health, education and standard of living; literacy rate, life expectancy and per capita income are all NOT among them, which is what makes the distractors plausible.

tags.exp: Lead and tin. The low melting point of the Pb-Sn eutectic is what lets solder join components without damaging them.

tags.sub: Chemistry: acids, bases, salts, metals and non-metals, common compounds

The Durand Cup, first played in 1888 at Simla - Asia's oldest football tournament and the third oldest in the world.
Karnam Malleswari, bronze in weightlifting at Sydney 2000 - the first Indian woman to win any Olympic medal. P.T. Usha famously missed bronze by 1/100th of a second in 1984, which is the trap.

Promotion of safe and mechanised cleaning of sewers and septic tanks by trained, certified workers. NAMASTE aims at eliminating hazardous manual entry - note it is urban sanitation labour, not urban infrastructure generally.
E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker - Periyar - who founded the Self-Respect Movement in Tamil Nadu in 1925 against caste and priestly domination.

tags.reason: An annual mathematics prize. The 2023 laureate is superseded by every later one.

tags.exp: The State Bank of India, which she chaired from 2013 to 2017 - the first woman to do so. A 'first' is settled once it happens, whoever holds the post now.
Endemic - constantly present at a predictable baseline in an area. An epidemic is a sharp rise above that baseline, and a pandemic an epidemic across continents.

tags.sub: Physical geography of India: relief, drainage, climate
tags.exp: Gujarat, at roughly 1,600 km - the longest coastline of any Indian state, thanks to the Kathiawar peninsula and the Gulfs of Kutch and Khambhat.
Tamil Nadu, at the tip of the Cauvery delta on the Bay of Bengal - a Ramsar wetland and wildlife sanctuary known for flamingos.

tags.sub: Inflation: types, measurement, WPI and CPI
tags.exp: Deflation - a fall in the general price level. Note the distinctions: disinflation is slowing inflation, devaluation is a fall in the currency's external value, and recession is falling output.

tags.sub: Geography of Mizoram: location, relief, rivers, climate, districts
tags.exp: Sedimentation. Mizoram's steep, deforested slopes and heavy monsoon shed large sediment loads that fill reservoirs and cut their live storage and turbine life. Deforestation is the underlying cause but sedimentation is the direct threat the question asks for.

tags.sub: Emerging technologies: AI, IoT, cloud, blockchain, 5G
tags.exp: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer. All three words matter: it is generative, it is PRE-trained, and it is a transformer - each distractor swaps exactly one.

tags.sub: Geography of Mizoram: location, relief, rivers, climate, districts
tags.exp: Palak Dil, in Siaha district - Mizoram's largest natural lake. Tam Dil is the better-known tourist lake and Rih Dil, though associated with Mizo folklore, lies across the border in Myanmar.

tags.sub: Christian missionaries, literacy and social change
tags.exp: 2001. Mizoram University was established by an Act of Parliament in 2000 and came into being on 2 July 2001, as a central university at Aizawl.
Tehri Dam on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand, about 260 m high - India's tallest. Sardar Sarovar is larger in volume and Hirakud far longer, so 'highest' is doing precise work here.

tags.sub: Gandhian movements: Non-cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India
tags.exp: Mahatma Gandhi.
Ravi Shankar, who won in 1968 for West Meets East with Yehudi Menuhin - the first Indian Grammy winner.
C.V. Raman, awarded the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for the Raman effect - the first Indian, and still the only one, to win it for work done in India. Chandrasekhar won in 1983 but as a US citizen.
Tokyo, whose greater metropolitan area is the world's most populous at around 37 million. Delhi is second on the UN's urban-agglomeration measure.

tags.sub: Economy and budget in the news

tags.exp: Myanmar. Operation Karuna delivered Indian relief after Cyclone Mocha struck in May 2023 - a completed humanitarian operation.
Reserving one-third of Lok Sabha and State Assembly seats for women. Introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill and enacted as the 106th Amendment - the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023.
China. SAARC's eight members are India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Afghanistan; China is only an observer.
100%. NESIDS is fully centrally funded, which is its defining feature - it exists precisely so North Eastern states need not find a matching share.
Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, who wrote Vande Mataram in 1875 and later placed it in his novel Anandamath. Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana, the national anthem - the pairing being tested.
Raja Ram Mohan Roy, founder of the Brahmo Sabha, campaigner against sati and for women's education, and conventionally called the father of the Indian Renaissance or of modern India.
M.K. Gandhi. The Story of My Experiments with Truth was written in Gujarati in the 1920s and covers his life to 1921.

MPSC keys Swami Dayananda, founder of the Arya Samaj and an early advocate of swarajya - 'India for Indians'. Worth knowing the sentiment is more often quoted from Dadabhai Naoroji, but he is not among the options.

The 42nd Amendment of 1976, which inserted 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' into the Preamble. The 44th (1978) reversed much of the rest of the 42nd, which is why it is the tempting wrong answer.

tags.sub: Union Executive: President, Vice-President, PM, Council of Ministers
tags.exp: 25 years. The Constitution sets no age for the Prime Minister directly; the PM must be a member of Parliament, and the Lok Sabha minimum is 25. For a Rajya Sabha route it would be 30.

tags.sub: Parliament: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, legislative procedure
tags.exp: Prorogation, which ends a session. Adjournment only suspends a sitting, adjournment sine die ends a sitting without a set date, and dissolution ends the life of the House itself.

tags.sub: Sixth Schedule and Autonomous District Councils
tags.exp: The Sixth Schedule, which provides Autonomous District Councils for tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram - Mizoram's being Chakma, Lai and Mara.
Majuli, in the Brahmaputra - the world's largest river island and India's first island district, notified in 2016.

tags.sub: Physical geography of India: relief, drainage, climate
tags.exp: The Hugli. The Damodar, once called Bengal's 'river of sorrow' for its floods, joins the Hugli distributary of the Ganga below Kolkata.
Narendra Modi, who called for a 'protein revolution' to follow the Green and White Revolutions by raising pulse and animal-protein output.
Badminton - the Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship. The women's equivalent is the Uber Cup.
Mike Tyson, nicknamed Kid Dynamite early in his career, and the youngest heavyweight champion at 20.
A transition zone between two biomes. Ecotones often hold species from both sides plus some of their own, which is the edge effect.

tags.sub: Physics: units and measurement, motion, force, work, energy, power
tags.exp: Friction. A conservative force does work independent of path and stores recoverable energy; friction dissipates it as heat, so the work done depends on the route taken.

tags.sub: Physics: units and measurement, motion, force, work, energy, power
tags.exp: That gravitational forces are non-conservative - the incorrect statement. Gravity IS conservative: it acts along the line joining two masses, is independent of the medium, and follows an inverse-square law, so the other three are all true.

tags.exp: Scattering of light by the particles of a colloid. Note the near-miss: option (a) says suspension. Colloidal particles are comparable to the wavelength of light, which is what makes the beam visible.

The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 - the full statutory title, giving effect to Article 21A. The three distractors are all plausible short forms, which is the point.

tags.exp: The stapes, in the middle ear - about 3 mm. The malleus and incus are the other two ear ossicles and are larger; the cochlea is not a bone at all.
Carlos Alcaraz, who won his first French Open in 2024, beating Alexander Zverev. A completed result does not change.

tags.exp: The 36th Amendment, 1975, which made Sikkim the 22nd state. The 35th had made it an associate state the year before.

The 44th Amendment, 1978, which removed the right to property from Part III and re-cast it as Article 300A, a mere legal right. Note the paper misprints this question's option letters as (a)(b)(c)(c).

A constitutional right. Voting comes from Article 326 and the Representation of the People Act, not from Part III, so it is neither a fundamental right nor merely statutory - the distinction the question exists to test.
Legal sanction. The Fundamental Duties in Article 51A are non-justiciable: no court can enforce them and no penalty attaches, so they carry moral and civic weight only.

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, called the Iron Man of India for integrating over 550 princely states into the Union as first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister.

tags.exp: The Attorney General of India, the government's chief legal adviser under Article 76. The Law Commission only recommends reform, and the CJI cannot advise the executive.
Education, moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment. Agriculture and police are State List; defence is Union List.

tags.sub: Parliament: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, legislative procedure
tags.exp: MPSC keys 'after the demand is granted' - that is, once the Lok Sabha has voted it. The technical distinction is that demands for grants are voted by the House and then authorised by the Appropriation Act.

The Chief Justice of the High Court. Article 159 requires a Governor to make the oath 'in the presence of the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State'. The President APPOINTS the Governor under Article 155 but does not administer the oath - that is the distinction being tested, and 'President' is the intended trap.

tags.sub: Judiciary: Supreme Court, High Courts, judicial review
tags.exp: Five - habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto - issued under Article 32 by the Supreme Court and Article 226 by the High Courts.

tags.sub: Parliament: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, legislative procedure
tags.exp: Yielding the floor. Crossing the floor is changing party allegiance and interpellation is the practice of questioning ministers, so both distractors are real terms for other things.
82.5 degrees E, the longitude through Mirzapur, taken as the Indian Standard Meridian and 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
Micro-plastics - fragments under 5 mm, from cosmetics, synthetic textiles and the breakdown of larger plastic. Nano-plastics are a further order smaller.

tags.sub: Physics: units and measurement, motion, force, work, energy, power
tags.exp: The coulomb - the SI unit of charge, one ampere-second. The ampere is the unit of current, which is the confusion being tested.
